root_cause.text: In rt2x00usb_probe(), the rt2x00 USB driver's usb_anchor devres allocation was incorrectly bound to the parent usb_device (`usb_dev->dev`) instead of the bound `usb_interface` (`usb_intf->dev`), causing the anchor to outlive driver unbind and leak resources when the interface was detached without physical device removal.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `devm_kmalloc(&usb_dev->dev, sizeof(struct usb_anchor), GFP_KERNEL)` to `devm_kmalloc(&usb_intf->dev, sizeof(struct usb_anchor), GFP_KERNEL)`, and the commit/CVE text explicitly states that USB drivers bind to interfaces and that the previous lifetime caused issues like memory leaks when drivers were unbound without device disconnection.

intent_record.intent_summary: Tie the managed allocation of rt2x00dev->anchor to the probed USB interface instead of the parent USB device so cleanup occurs with the correct device lifecycle.
intent_record.what: The first argument passed to devm_kmalloc() in rt2x00usb_probe() was changed from &usb_dev->dev to &usb_intf->dev when allocating memory for rt2x00dev->anchor.
intent_record.how: This makes the managed allocation for rt2x00dev->anchor be tied to the USB interface device rather than the USB device, so its lifetime and automatic cleanup follow the interface being probed and removed.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement binds the managed allocation of rt2x00dev->anchor to the parent usb_device devres context via &usb_dev->dev instead of the probed usb_interface device, causing the allocation to survive interface unbind and leak until physical device removal.
